author: 朱四欢
title_status: Finalize the title after the full-network implementation and DecontX analyses; do not impose the conclusion anticipated by a proposed title.
introduction: Ligand–receptor inference converts cell-type expression profiles into candidate interactions and relative priorities. Cross-cohort evaluation consequently involves two related but distinct questions: whether an expression-based interaction score changes in the same direction after a perturbation, and whether the corresponding candidate gains or loses relative priority in another study. These contrasts operate on different scales and can involve different eligible interactions and network backgrounds. Agreement at one stage therefore warrants direct evaluation at subsequent stages. Distinguishing these quantities is particularly useful when a candidate list is intended to guide biological follow-up, because reproducible expression availability and reproducible prioritization represent different properties of the analysis. [@Dimitrov2022][@Dimitrov2024]

Previous benchmarks have examined interaction resources, scoring methods, differential communication inference and spatial support, including reproducibility across samples or tissue sections. [@Cesaro2025][@Ku2026] Building on this work, an informative disease-specific assessment should compare representations on the same candidates, preserve the biological sampling unit, and identify which analytic choices account for changes in agreement. Such an assessment also requires a relevant null reference: ligand–receptor candidates share genes, so their concordance indicators cannot be treated as independent trials. Preserving each sample's complete score vector while reallocating treatment labels provides a way to retain this dependence. In parallel, explicit interventions on score representation and ranking procedures can distinguish an observed reproducibility gap from explanations that have not been directly tested.

Experimental cerebral ischemia provides a traceable setting for this assessment. Public studies contain acute ischemic and sham-operated mouse brain samples with astrocytes and endothelial cells, while differing in tissue sampling, cellular composition and replication. [@Zheng2022][@Ruan2023] These cells offer a focused pair of interacting lineages, and barrier-related transcription supplies a biologically relevant context for their responses. The same setting also makes identity uncertainty and contaminating transcripts consequential: apparent expression of a candidate ligand may depend on which cells are assigned to the sending population.

Here, we assess cross-cohort reproducibility along the path from expression coavailability to relative ligand–receptor priority. We use animal-level contrasts in two primary cohorts, a dependence-preserving label-allocation baseline, independent-reference cell-selection checks, and an ambient-RNA sensitivity protocol. We additionally examine the installed aggregation implementation and the membership of its ranking universe, with the affected quantities held constant at each intervention. A third cohort with author-reported biological replication, together with supplementary sorted and spatial datasets, provides descriptive extensions. The objective is to identify reproducible features and sources of sensitivity in this specific inference workflow, while providing an auditable basis for subsequent validation.

LIANA developers merged a correction for repeated ranking of shared score columns on 9 September 2026 in [LIANA PR #261](https://github.com/scverse/liana/pull/261). We use this known correction as a controlled intervention to quantify its consequences in ischemia cohorts and the remaining dependence on ranking context.
methods_design: The two animal-resolved cohorts comprised GSE174574, with three sham and three middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) libraries at 24 h, and GSE245386, with three sham and two newly generated wild-type MCAO libraries. Lrg1-knockout libraries and reused GSE174574 data were excluded from GSE245386. The latter study used 60 min of occlusion followed by 24 h of reperfusion, approximately 1 h later when time is measured from ischemia onset. GSM records, sample titles, filenames and source articles were reconciled, including the 2025 correction to GSE245386. The animal represented by each original library was the disease-comparison unit. [@Zheng2022][@Ruan2023][@RuanCorrection2025]

An updated GEO search returned 145 GDS records; complete SOFT metadata and source articles were examined for 21 additional candidates. Queries, retrieved records and exclusion reasons were retained. This targeted update was not treated as an exhaustive systematic review. GSE332910 supplied sham and 24-h RNA libraries from ipsilateral striatum after 60-min MCAO and 24-h reperfusion. Supplementary Table S1 reports three biological replicates and three libraries per group. The number of mice contributing to each library, including whether samples were pooled, remained unspecified. Its single-nucleus assay, region and platform differed from the original cohorts. Under the revision-stage plan, this extension remained descriptive, with library-level effects and no P values, and was kept outside the original two-cohort permutation analysis. Corresponding ATAC libraries were not additional replicates. [@Zhang2026]

Submitted matrices were processed separately by library. Quality control retained cells or nuclei with 200–6,000 detected genes, at least 500 UMIs and at most 20% mitochondrial UMIs; duplicate gene symbols were summed. A fixed marker rule assigned astrocytes, endothelial cells and competing broad lineages, retaining unassigned cells. This rule was transferred unchanged to the third cohort. In the two original cohorts, all retained cells were additionally annotated with the independently trained CellTypist whole-mouse-brain model; an isocortex/hippocampus model provided a reference sensitivity check. Best-match prediction was used without majority voting. [@Dominguez2022][@Yao2021][@Yao2023]

Scrublet was run per original library with expected doublet rate 0.05, simulated-to-observed ratio 2, 30 principal components, exact neighbors, automatic thresholds and seed 20260910. [@Wolock2019] The principal selections were the original marker assignment and its intersection with an agreeing whole-brain reference label, maximum sigmoid score ≥0.5 and no predicted doublet. Reference scores were treated as classifier outputs rather than calibrated correctness probabilities. Marker panels, label mappings, confidence distributions, simulated doublet scores and thresholds were retained for audit.

For rule assignment, marker log1p(CP10k) values were standardized across QC-passing cells within each library using a population-standard-deviation floor of 0.25, clipped to −3 to 10, and averaged within each lineage panel. Assignment required the highest mean score ≥0.5, a margin ≥0.25 over the second-highest panel, and at least two detected markers; remaining cells were unassigned. Astrocyte markers were Aldh1l1, Slc1a3, Slc1a2, Gja1, Glul, Sox9 and Aldoc; endothelial markers were Pecam1, Cdh5, Esam, Tek, Erg, Vwf and Kdr. Fixed panels for the other 13 competing lineages are retained in marker_panel.json. These are operational rule labels.
methods_scores: The fixed mouseconsensus resource contained 3,989 records. Directed candidates were evaluated from astrocytes to endothelial cells and in the reverse direction. For each animal, expression coavailability was the square root of the product of ligand and receptor mean log1p(CP10k), calculated within sender and receiver populations. Complex expression and detection were represented by the minimum constituent value. The original 10% gate required minimum-subunit detection ≥10% in at least two animals in either condition, assessed separately for ligand and receptor; 5% and 20% gates were retained as sensitivities. Disease effects were equal-animal MCAO means minus sham means.

LIANA 1.10.0 rank_aggregate ran CellPhoneDB, Connectome, log2FC, NATMI and SingleCellSignalR separately within each original library, using the same resource, expr_prop=0.1, min_cells=30, n_perms=100, seed=20260910, n_jobs=1 and return_all_lrs=False. [@Dimitrov2022][@Dimitrov2024] The complete network among assigned lineages with at least 30 retained cells was computed before extracting the two target directions. The reference-supported selection removed predicted doublets from all lineages and additionally required reference agreement for the target populations. Normalization used each cell's total across all submitted genes.

Metrics were grouped by interpretation. Coavailability, lr_means, expr_prod and lrscore were related expression-oriented summaries. Connectome and NATMI shared expr_prod, and the five interfaces contributed three distinct magnitude columns: lr_means, expr_prod and lrscore. Relative priority was represented by 1−magnitude_rank. Here magnitude_rank is a bounded robust rank aggregation (RRA) score, not a simple percentile rank; larger transformed values indicate higher relative priority. Within-library cell-label permutation P values were kept separate from animal-level disease inference. Unreported scores were retained as missing rather than replaced with zero.

The main comparison used the same directed candidates with finite values for all five metrics in every one of the 11 animals. This complete-case intersection was defined without treatment labels or an additional group-dependent coavailability gate. Concordance was reported as same nonzero-sign effects divided by all common candidates and, separately, by candidates with nonzero effects in both cohorts. Absolute effects ≤10^-12 were numerical zeros; zero–zero pairs did not count as concordant. Spearman correlation included all common candidates. A separate descriptive transform used within-animal average-tie percentile ranks over the same fixed target set before calculating disease effects. This target-only transform was distinguished from full-network RRA.
methods_null: The null baseline retained each animal's entire multivariate score vector and exhaustively reassigned condition labels within studies. The three-versus-three and two-versus-three allocations generated 20×10=200 joint configurations, including the observed assignment. Genes, interaction edges and individual cells were not independently shuffled. Per-animal scores could be reused because normalization, reference selection and within-library LIANA scoring had not used disease labels. Both concordance fractions and Spearman correlation were recalculated for every configuration. A separate coavailability analysis reconstructed all gene-covered resource edges and reapplied the original group-dependent 10% gate within each allocation, including the candidate-selection step in its null distribution.

One-sided exact upper-tail P values equaled the fraction of the 200 statistics at least as large as observed, with comparison tolerance 10^-12. No Monte Carlo correction or artificial extra permutations were added. Null means, medians and 2.5th–97.5th percentiles were reported; the percentiles describe a label-randomization reference interval, not a confidence interval for observed concordance. Three Holm families were specified before computing these outputs: A, two selections×five metrics×three statistics, totaling 30 tests; B, two selections×four expression-minus-native-priority gaps×three statistics, totaling 24 tests; and C, two selections×three dynamically gated coavailability statistics, totaling six exploratory tests. Adjusted P values retain their family labels. The gap null concerns treatment-label association, not equivalence between algorithms. Exchangeability within each study remains an assumption. Revision-stage plans followed inspection of the earlier manuscript's results and were not preregistered.

After the joint results were known, a dated supplementary diagnostic fixed one cohort's observed labels and reassigned only the other cohort's labels. The saved joint configurations provided all 20 discovery-only and 10 validation-only allocations for every fixed metric and dynamically gated statistic. Complete distributions and unadjusted one-sided exact tails were reported without altering families A–C or creating a new confirmatory family. Joint randomization tests the null of no treatment association in either cohort under exchangeability; rejecting it does not establish treatment association separately in both cohorts. The conditional diagnostic retains the validation design's minimum attainable P value of 0.10. It therefore addresses the interpretation of the joint baseline rather than resolving limited biological replication.
methods_implementation: An implementation audit examined the installed aggregation code and its tagged upstream source. A deterministic four-row example directly invoked the official function to assess successive ranking of the expr_prod column shared by Connectome and NATMI. Full networks were then recomputed for all original libraries under both selections. Target scores and native consensus outputs were compared with the earlier exports after identical TSV serialization. On each unchanged full-network score table, each distinct magnitude column was then ranked once and passed to the same RRA function. [@Kolde2012] This explicitly named unique-column diagnostic preserved the installed package and native outputs; it was not designated an official corrected release.

A subsequent background diagnostic intersected all directed cell-type–ligand–receptor edges with finite magnitude scores across the 11 complete networks, including non-target cell-type pairs. Each distinct magnitude column was ranked once within this fixed global universe, RRA was applied, and the same original target intersection was extracted after verifying its inclusion. The intervention changed ranking-universe membership while preserving upstream expression scores and their original cellular context. Stored float32 magnitude precision was restored before aggregation, and both native and unique-column full-network scores were reconstructed as checks. Average-tie ranks of expr_prod and lrscore were compared for exact and approximate redundancy. Rank saturation, ties, zero disease effects and both concordance denominators were reported. These implementation and universe diagnostics were descriptive additions; no new inferential P values were calculated or transferred from null families A–C.

We additionally retrieved the aggregation function at the fixed merge commit d4211373692e7b9c10210488ccb1efe06452b097 of [LIANA PR #261](https://github.com/scverse/liana/pull/261), retained source and SHA256, and executed it independently on all 22 raw complete networks for elementwise comparison with our unique-column diagnostic. This checks the aggregation function only, not a full newer pipeline release. The resource, explicit expr_prop=0.1 and expression scores were held unchanged; concurrent upstream changes to default detection thresholds were therefore excluded.
methods_ambient: The ambient-RNA sensitivity protocol applies decontX 1.10.0 in R 4.6.1/Bioconductor 3.23 separately to each of the 11 original QC-passing libraries. Existing whole-brain reference broad labels for all cells define clusters, without confidence filtering or re-estimation from corrected data. Settings are background=NULL, batch=NULL, delta=c(10,10), estimateDelta=TRUE, maxIter=500, convergence=0.001 and seed=20260911. DecontX estimates contamination from filtered cells without requiring empty droplets; its estimates remain conditional on clustering and mixture-model assumptions. [@Yang2020] Per-library iteration logs and convergence status are retained rather than assumed.

Continuous nonnegative corrected counts preserve cell and gene order. Under unchanged cell selections, expression summaries and full-network native and diagnostic priorities use corrected totals across all genes as the normalization denominator. Detection in the custom coavailability gate is evaluated as estimated count >0, with estimated count ≥1 reported separately because corrected values can be fractional. LIANA retains the float32 normalized representation used in the raw pipeline. Positive-entry counts before and after conversion are recorded, and explicit numerical zeros are removed before its getnnz-based sparse expression proportions are calculated, enforcing a >0 detection rule. The ≥1 criterion is a custom expression-eligibility sensitivity, not rounding into observed UMIs. Nonpositive totals trigger an audit failure instead of reuse of raw totals. Candidate losses and common eligible sets are reported. Fractional estimates are not supplied to DESeq2; ambient correction and aggregation implementation remain separate interventions.
methods_auxiliary: GSE163752 provided six matched ipsilateral–contralateral comparisons, with three or four mice contributing to each sample pool. Only astrocyte and endothelial samples with consistent metadata mappings were used. Submitted replicate identifiers defined pairing. Author-normalized values were transformed as log2(x+1); mean paired differences and pointwise 95% t intervals with five degrees of freedom summarized expression support. [@Spitzer2022] These intervals were not simultaneous significance decisions, and contralateral tissue was not equated with sham. Earlier transcriptome-wide tests and BH results were retained in the audit record without using them as the criterion for this descriptive summary.

Barrier-related transcription provided supplementary cell-state context. Raw counts were summed by animal and cell type, requiring at least 30 cells; genes with at least 10 counts in as many animals as the smaller group size were analyzed with PyDESeq2 using design ~condition. All fixed-panel genes and full test results were retained. [@Love2014][@Muzellec2023][@Vanlandewijck2018][@Munji2019] GSE233814 contributed five section records to a supplementary expression figure using verified spatial coordinates. Spots were not animal replicates, unverified infarct regions were not assigned, and spatial associations were treated as descriptive context. [@Zucha2024]
